profiles.name: CRANK
profiles.tagline: SHORT GAME GOT THE WRENCH, DRIVER GOT FIRING SQUAD
profiles.profile: CRANK is basically a one-man demolition derby with a wedge. The pattern is ugly but real: the tee game keeps coughing up blood, then the scrambling and putter drag the carcass back to the clubhouse before the round fully faceplants. That’s why the card keeps living in that annoying little space where the gross golf looks leaky but the net results keep showing up anyway. When the irons cooperate, he can absolutely steal one; when they don’t, it turns into a survival film with sand saves and grimy par saves doing the heavy lifting.

profiles.name: MattF
profiles.tagline: TEE BALL WITH A BODYGUARD AND A PUTTER THAT PAYS RENT
profiles.profile: MattF is the kind of file that makes the rest of the league resentfully mutter, yeah, that checks out. The driver is loud, the approach play is tidy, and the scoring clubs keep showing up like they’re on a payroll. He can get cute with the ball-striking mix and still walk out with a result because there’s enough juice everywhere else to cover the weird holes. The only real problem is that this profile is so clean it’s almost rude: when he’s not winning, he’s usually just sitting there looking like he should be.

profiles.name: KeithK75
profiles.tagline: GREEN-FINDER WITH A HAMMER AND ZERO APOLOGIES
profiles.profile: KeithK75 is the league’s problem child in the best possible way: the ball screams, the approaches are filthy, and the whole operation is built on hitting enough greens that the rest of us can only stare and hate. He doesn’t need a pretty round to ruin yours; he just keeps piling up quality golf until the math gets embarrassing. The profile is strong enough that the occasional messy patch barely matters, because the baseline is still “show up, hit a bunch of greens, collect.” This is the kind of guy who makes a course look underfed and underprepared.

profiles.name: Dan94
profiles.tagline: TEE SHOTS FOR DAYS, BRAIN CELLS OPTIONAL
profiles.profile: Dan94 is built like a live grenade with a laser rangefinder. The long game is the headline, and when the irons are cooperating he can make a course look stupid in a hurry, but there’s enough volatility in the rest of the package that every round feels like it might either print money or set the leaderboard on fire for the wrong reasons. The ceiling is obviously filthy; the issue is that the whole operation can still lurch around like it’s being steered by a raccoon with a Red Bull habit. Still, when this one clicks, it’s violent.

profiles.name: BigTime
profiles.profile: BigTime is a classic “don’t ask how it got here, just watch the irons” file. The approaches are carrying the whole economy, and that’s enough to keep him in the mix even when the driver and putter are acting like they’ve never met the rest of the bag. There’s some genuine ceiling here because the middle of the bag can get red-hot fast, but the profile still has a little chaos tax attached to it. He’s the guy who can float a round on shotmaking and then immediately make you sweat with a few too many sloppy extras.

profiles.name: HamSammich
profiles.tagline: CHAOS FOOD, CHAOS GOLF, SAME MENU
profiles.profile: HamSammich is golf played with a butter knife and a bad decision. There’s enough pop in spots to make you think the round is turning around, and then the short-game leaks or the big number shows up and reminds everyone this thing is still held together with tape. The evidence says volatile, which is a polite way of saying he can look passable for stretches and then suddenly turn a normal scorecard into a crime scene. If there’s a recurring identity here, it’s that the round never really stays on the rails for long.
